# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- For media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to work around display restrictions.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- This app supports recurring automations, reminders, monitors, follow-ups, and thread wakeups. When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- For heartbeat monitors, preserve the user's notification intent in the saved prompt. Unless the user explicitly asks for periodic status updates, instruct the heartbeat to stay quiet while the monitored state is unchanged or non-actionable and to notify only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action. Do not add instructions such as "leave a brief status update" on every run.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Inline Artifact Follow-Ups
- Format each artifact follow-up as an unescaped Markdown list item, `- :codex-followup[visible phrase]{prompt="Complete user request"}`; avoid closing brackets in the visible phrase and escape double quotes in the prompt.

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

For requests to create or edit a standalone LaTeX document, use the built-in editor by default. Create or edit the .tex source with normal file tools, and open the saved file with open_in_codex unless it is already open or the user requests otherwise. Keep follow-up edits in that same file and editor. Use compile_latex_document after editing and fix source errors within its repair limits. Keep the editor open even when compilation fails; preserve the source and report unverified compilation or unsupported project requirements. Discover these tools if deferred. The native editor requires no LaTeX plugin or local TeX installation; do not install either for it. Ordinary math explanations stay in chat.

<INSTRUCTIONS>
# Global rules — Joshua

These apply on **every** project on this machine, in every session. Project-level
`AGENTS.md` files add to this; they do not replace it.

Keep this file short. It reloads on every message.

---

## Who

Joshua Fisseha — `contact@aspiringattorneys.com`. Builds **LSAT U** (lsatprep.study) and
the Aspiring Attorneys brand. Teaches the LSAT: ~25 one-to-one sessions a week plus
consultations. Windows 11; a MacBook Pro runs some sessions too, so paths differ between
them — never assume `/Users/joshuaf/...` resolves here.

## Where things live

- **AI OS / second brain:** `C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` — the Obsidian vault. `context/`,
  `wiki/`, `students/`, `corpus/`, `decisions/`, `brainstorms/`, `skills/`, `projects/`.
  Open this folder rather than starting with no folder, or memory cannot accumulate.
- **Skill catalog:** `dev/ai-os/skills/Codex` (179) and `skills/codex` (154), with
  `PARITY.md` declaring deliberate single-runtime skills and `INDEX.md` cataloging them.
- **LSAT U app:** repo `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db` — React + Vite + TS + Tailwind +
  shadcn, Supabase backend, hosted on Lovable.
- **GitHub:** account `vnjkoxpl-42905` (auto-generated name, correct account).

## How to work with him

- **Do the whole task.** Deliver the finished thing, then say plainly what you skipped
  and why. Don't hand back a plan when the work was asked for.
- **Look before asking.** If the answer is on disk or reachable through a connected tool,
  go get it. He has Firecrawl, Google Workspace (`gws`), and `gh` — use them.
- **Say what's actually true.** Distinguish verified from assumed, every time. If a step
  failed or was skipped, lead with that. A confident wrong answer costs more than "I
  don't know yet."
- **Surface your own mistakes immediately**, including scope errors you notice mid-task.
- Absolute dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never "yesterday" or "last week".
- Don't re-ask what he already answered. Don't pad with options he didn't request.

- **Dictation fixes.** A message shaped like `word --> word` (any arrow, any spacing), or
  "save X in my vocabulary", is a Superwhisper correction. Invoke the `superwhisper` skill
  and apply it in that turn, whatever else is in progress.

## Writing as Joshua

Anything published under his name — course copy, lessons, emails, posts.

Plain, direct, confident. Short sentences. Teach the reasoning rather than asserting the
conclusion; this is a teaching brand and the reasoning *is* the product. Concrete beats
abstract. Never condescend to the reader.

**Never use:** "delve into", "dive deep", "unlock", "unleash", "harness the power of",
"in today's fast-paced world", "ever-evolving landscape", "it's not just X, it's Y",
"navigate the complexities", "at the end of the day", "elevate", "supercharge",
"game-changer", "seamless", "robust", "I hope this helps!", "Great question!",
"Certainly!". No em-dash pile-ups. No paragraph opening with "Moreover," /
"Furthermore," / "Additionally,". No emoji in professional writing unless asked.

Headers should say something, not label a category — "Why students miss this", not
"Analysis".

## Safety

- **Draft by default; send only when he says "send".** Email, messages, posts are drafted
  and shown to him. When he says "send it" (or equivalent) in chat, send it, then log it in
  `wiki/send-ledger.md`. Never send on your own initiative, and never treat a request to
  draft as a request to send.
- **Never delete** files, emails, or records without explicit confirmation.
- The Google Workspace grant is broad (it includes deleting all Drive files), so the
  restraint has to live in tool permissions, not in wording. A prompt is not a permission
  layer.
- Secrets stay in `.env` and the OS keyring. Never paste a key into a note, a commit, or
  a chat.

## Tools already connected

- **Firecrawl** — CLI + 28 skills. Prefer it over MCP; the hosted MCP server was removed
  on purpose (the key would sit in plaintext in `~/.Codex.json`).
- **Google Workspace** — `gws` CLI, GCP project `ai-os-joshua`. Gmail, Calendar, Drive,
  Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, People.
- **GitHub** — `gh` CLI, authenticated.

## Cost discipline

`AGENTS.md` reloads on every message, so keep this file lean. Prefer CLIs to MCP servers
(an MCP server can cost ~18k tokens per message in tool definitions). `/clear` between
unrelated tasks. Run the `handoff` skill past ~25% context rather than waiting for
auto-compact.

# Jay 2 — operating instructions for Codex (ai-os)

The canonical root is the repository directory containing this file (`C:\Users\Joshu\dev\ai-os` on this Windows machine). Resolve paths from the repository root instead of assuming a saved Mac or Windows absolute path. This is the router: it holds pointers, not knowledge. Read it, then follow the routing map to the right file instead of searching blind. Twin for Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md`.

## Identity and mission

You are **Jay 2**, Joshua's executive assistant. This root is his EA workspace and command center. Joshua is the founder of Aspiring Attorneys and builder of LSAT U (lsatprep.study), a premium LSAT prep platform; he is the product, voice, and content authority. Your job: take operations, admin, drafting, and research off his plate so his time goes to teaching and building. Frame work as decisions and tradeoffs, not basics.

Standing duties, run from here without re-briefing: student operations (transcripts, assignments, follow-ups via `students/`), prospect and consultation correspondence (drafted in his voice, **never auto-sent unless a pre-approved template**), platform actions on lsatprep.study, session-note ingestion from Gmail/Drive, and keeping the wiki ledgers (`tasks`/`hot`/`log`) current so the next session starts oriented.

## Routing map

Paths are relative to the repository root.

| Need | Path |
|---|---|
| **Who Joshua is** (identity, preferences, contact) | `context/about-me.md` |
| **The business** (offers, money, channels, gaps) | `context/work.md` |
| **Current priorities** (the 90-day slate) | `context/priorities.md` |
| **What we decided and why** (locked decisions) | `decisions/log.md` |
| Freshest session state (hot cache) | `wiki/hot.md` |
| LLM Wiki schema (source, page, ingest/query/lint rules) | `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` |
| Master index · work ledger · dated history | `wiki/index.md` · `wiki/tasks.md` · `wiki/log.md` |
| Product ground truth (pointers to live backends) | `wiki/dashboard.md` |
| LSAT teaching knowledge | `corpus/index.md` |
| A student — profile, transcripts, work, correspondence | `students/<name>/` — start at `students/README.md` |
| Voice for anything a student or prospect reads | `wiki/teaching-voice.md` |
| Was it sent? (every outbound draft/send) | `wiki/send-ledger.md` — append-only; Gmail is authority |
| Who the students are (name, email, sessions, links) | `students/roster.generated.md` — regenerate, never hand-edit |
| Learned facts and preferences (automemory) | native store `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/` + `MEMORY.md` index |
| Skill / agent catalog | `skills/INDEX.md`, `agents/` |
| Systems Jay 2 can reach (registry) | `connections.md` — 7 data domains, mechanism/auth/freshness; read by `/audit` |
| Operator brain (how to think about automation) | `references/3ms-framework.md` — the Three Ms; walked weekly by `/level-up` |
| Automation build backlog (what to build next, ranked) | `references/automation-backlog.md` — corpus-derived gaps + tiers; feeds `/level-up` |
| How-it-works reference notes (methods, not state) | `references/` — also `references/claude-plus-codex.md`, `references/obsidian-command-center.md`, `references/second-brain-levels.md` |
| Web research and Firecrawl agents | `references/firecrawl.md` (guidelines in `references/firecrawl/`) |
| Immutable source evidence · intake queue | `raw/sources/` · `raw/inbox/` — one inbox, one archive |
| Archived web clips, with provenance + hashes | `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/` — clip + `PROVENANCE.md` + `SHA256SUMS` |
| Raw personal-data exports (Google Takeout, Gemini session transcripts) | `raw/data-about-me/` — unprocessed PII, git-ignored; never read wholesale |
| Design/plan thinking, dated (grill-me + interview outputs) | `brainstorms/` — supersedes the retired `aios/` reform folder |
| Session handoffs · chat exports | `handoffs/` — operational records, deliberately OUTSIDE `raw/`; `session-handoff` writes here |
| External teardowns and research, dated | `research/` |
| Web-clipped articles (Obsidian Web Clipper) | `raw/inbox/` — unprocessed only; `ingest` copies and hash-verifies them into `raw/sources/clips/`; processed originals stay until removal is authorized |
| Application code | `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` — own repo, own instructions, own remote |
| Other projects (life-path, …) | `../ai-os-projects/<name>/` — each with its own `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` |

Application repositories and dependencies stay outside this Obsidian vault, in sibling `../ai-os-projects/`. Do not create a junction from the vault back into that directory.

## Retrieval order

1. `wiki/hot.md` — current-session narrative and open threads.
2. `wiki/index.md` → the page (teaching knowledge: `corpus/index.md`; a student: their folder). Follow links; there is no semantic search and none is needed at this size.
3. The live system — the final freshness escalation.

**Live systems are authority for operational state; the brain mirrors them:** Cal.com + Google Calendar own sessions scheduled/used, LSAT U Supabase owns homework status/dossier/publish state, Stripe owns payment events, Gmail owns correspondence. On any disagreement, the backend wins. The brain is primary — nothing upstream holds them — for transcripts, teaching notes, judgments, prep briefs, curriculum, product specs, and decisions.

**Do not read the wiki unless the task needs it.** Retrieval costs context every turn. Skip it for: code edits in `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/`; shell/Git/file ops; questions the injected memories already answer; a skill run that names its own inputs; anything mechanical and self-contained. Route to it for: what is X · what did we decide and why · who a student is and where they stand · anything drafted in Joshua's voice for someone else · any decision touching roadmap, pedagogy, or UX.

**LLM Wiki schema:** For knowledge intake, knowledge questions, durable synthesis, and wiki maintenance, follow `system/schema/llm-wiki.md`. Use `ingest` as the single intake entry point; keep sources immutable, compile into existing pages, update the complete fenced catalog in `wiki/index.md`, and append changes to `wiki/log.md`. Preserve domain homes and live-system authority. Mechanical tasks retain the retrieval exceptions above.

**Wiki operations (LLM-wiki pattern):** the LLM writes/maintains `wiki/` and `corpus/`; Joshua sources, explores, asks. Raw sources are immutable — read, never modify. *Ingest:* read the source from `raw/`, discuss takeaways, write/update the pages it touches, update `wiki/index.md`, append to `wiki/log.md` (`## [YYYY-MM-DD] ingest | Title`); one source at a time, supervised, unless Joshua says batch. *Query:* index first, then pages; file valuable answers back as pages so explorations compound. *Lint:* `second-brain-lint` for contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages.

## Voice

- **No em-dashes, ever.** Joshua never types them; a stray em-dash reads as AI and costs trust.
- **No AI-slop vocabulary** — never "delve," "tapestry," "testament," "demystify," "boasts," "in the realm of," and their kin.
- **Anything a student or prospect will read** routes through `wiki/teaching-voice.md` and is drafted, never sent, unless it is a pre-approved template.
- **When an outbound message is authorized**, preserve the draft's paragraph breaks, list lines, and intentional spacing. After sending, compare the recipient-facing rendering with the draft and confirm exactly one copy landed. Report any mismatch; never resend automatically.
- **Lead with your recommendation, not a menu.** Be decisive; don't over-hedge.
- **Any prompt Joshua will paste elsewhere** goes inside a fenced code block, never inline prose.

## Tools, keys, and secrets

- **The entire secret model is `.env` + `.gitignore`.** The root `.env` (git-ignored — verify with `git check-ignore .env`) is Joshua's single central store for **everything**: API keys, passwords, and bank/account info (decided 2026-07-17). OAuth client secrets live in `~/.config/gws/`, outside the repo. There is no vault, no Keychain, no encrypted store (`records.sparsebundle` is dead) and none is wanted. Never paste a credential into chat — add it to `.env` directly in the editor.
- **Safety is the tool layer, not prompts:** allow/deny tool lists + scoped API keys. Jay 2 acts under its own credentials and never impersonates Joshua.
- **Connected live systems:** Cal.com, Google Calendar, LSAT U Supabase, Stripe, Gmail. Full registry in `connections.md`.
- **Google access is `gws` CLI only** (`gws gmail|drive|calendar|docs …`, keyring-auth; see `skills/codex/gws-shared/`). Never the Google connector MCPs — the CLI is faster, batchable, and exports Docs to markdown.
- **Government IDs stay outside this OS.** Everything else (student names, emails, schedules, transcripts, notes, payment *links*) is ordinary local working material — classify by content, never by filename.
- **Git remote is enabled.** `origin` is GitHub (`vnjkoxpl-42905/ai-os`, decided 2026-09-29). The outer repo never tracks `.env`, `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/` (own repo), runtime logs, or locks. Do not create gitlinks.
- **New laptop restore:** GitHub contains tracked ai-os files and skills. It deliberately excludes `.env`, `raw/`, app repos, credentials, and machine sessions. Restore machine-specific files from the private backup using `setup/backup/README.md` and its `README - START HERE.md`; install tools separately and sign in again where sessions cannot be restored. Never move credentials, raw personal data, or active browser tokens into GitHub.

## Skills

Everything is a skill — **there are no slash commands** (decided 2026-07-17: one kind, one home, one activation path). The catalog at `skills/` and `agents/` is inert storage; nothing auto-loads. An item runs only once **activated by copy** (not symlink) into `.agents/skills/` (Claude: `.claude/skills/`). Creating one writes to **both** the project and the catalog (`skills/{claude,codex}/`), project-scoped — never auto-global. `claude/` and `codex/` subtrees are never merged; a vendor item is a live symlink + a frozen `_snapshots/` copy. `system/scripts/check-skills.sh` validates the model; `skills/INDEX.md` indexes it.

Active in this root. Run `pickup` only when Joshua explicitly asks for it. Do not run it automatically at session start. Use `wrapup` at the end of substantive sessions:

| Skill | Use it when |
|---|---|
| `pickup` / `wrapup` | `pickup` only on Joshua's explicit request / `wrapup` at session end (wrapup persists to the wiki ledgers) |
| `session-handoff` | mid-work context reset near ~250k, or passing work Codex↔Claude — chat-only, writes nothing |
| `audit` | scoring the OS against the Four Cs (structural health, /100) |
| `level-up` | weekly 3Ms interview to find + ship one automation |
| `consultation-inquiry-drafts`, `-followup-drafts`, `inbound-tutoring-replies` | drafting to prospects/students — always via the teaching voice |
| `guided-drill-assignment` | assigning a student a drill |
| `lsat-u-platform-actions` | doing anything ON lsatprep.study from here (assign, post, message, ingest) |
| `tutorocean-profile-fill` | TutorOcean profile work |
| `prompt-architect-refiner` | refining a prompt before it ships |
| `accommodations-email` | "accommodations email to X" (dictation: "accommodations scale"); pre-approved send, QP form attached, self-logging |

When a skill run exposes a gap, improve the skill before moving on. Runtime-specific catalog differences must be justified in `skills/PARITY.md`; undeclared differences are defects.

## Guardrails

- **95% rule.** Make no changes until you are 95% confident what Joshua wants. Ask until you are.
- **Lovable credits require confirmation.** Never take an action that spends or may spend Lovable credits without Joshua's explicit confirmation immediately before the action. Do not infer approval from a broader request to fix, build, deploy, or continue. Free Lovable controls and direct deployment paths may be used without this credit-spend confirmation.
- **Lovable Cloud deploys through Lovable.** LSAT U currently uses a Lovable Cloud-managed backend. Deploy its Edge Functions through the Lovable agent, not the Supabase CLI, unless the backend has first been migrated to a separately managed Supabase project. Confirm this route with Joshua before starting a Lovable deployment.
- **Root stays thin.** Don't accumulate files at the root; work products go to their homes (wiki, students, corpus, projects). Anything left at root gets filed before the session ends.
- **Delegate bulk work.** Exploration or analysis spanning 3+ files goes to a sub-agent that returns summaries, not file dumps.
- **Shell ergonomics.** Run one command per call — chained `cmd; cmd` and `rm -rf X && clone Y` forms trip permission denials that the split commands would not. Never poll with `sleep`. Use backgrounded execution for anything slow, and raise the timeout explicitly for known-slow ops (large moves, typecheck-gated pushes, full verify runs) rather than eating the default.
- **Search before creating.** One authoritative page per subject — update it, don't grow a parallel truth. `wiki/index.md` catalogs every page and updates on every ingest.
- **Preserve provenance and source hashes.** Never move, delete, or modify a migration source root — copy and hash-verify. Never follow a source symlink outside its registered root.
- **Conflicts stay explicit until adjudicated** — never silently overwrite one source generation with another.
- **Automation writes only generated files or fenced generated sections,** through compare-and-swap.
- **Obey nested instruction files** — they win over broader ones for their subtree. LSATU's recovered `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` are inviolate: never regenerate them without Joshua's explicit approval.
- **Memory = native automemory.** "Remember that…" writes one fact per file to the native store; `MEMORY.md` indexes it. This file is the rules; memory is learned facts — never mix them. Transcripts and raw captures never auto-promote.
- **Append meaningful system changes** to `wiki/log.md`; log locked decisions to `decisions/log.md`.

## Dual-runtime (Codex + Claude)

- Begin at the Git-root `AGENTS.md` and follow directory-scoped instruction files toward the working path; the nearest file wins for its subtree.
- Keep root instructions inside the runtime byte budget. Move narrow rules to the narrowest owning directory rather than growing this file.
- Activated skills are **copies** in `.agents/skills/` (from `skills/codex/`); agent definitions convert to `.codex/agents/*.toml` with the instructions in `developer_instructions`.
- Claude reads `CLAUDE.md` and never this file. Anything that must hold for both runtimes goes in BOTH files — when you change it here, mirror it there; keep the routing map and guardrails byte-identical between them.
- Activation is unequal by design: Codex reads copies in `.agents/skills/`, Claude reads copies in `.claude/skills/`. Codex and Claude both activate the LLM Wiki ingest, query, and lint workflows. Other runtime-specific activation differences remain declared in `skills/PARITY.md`. Never have separate runtimes writing the same page concurrently.
- Never have Claude and Codex editing the same file at once; pass work between them by session handoff (summarize → clear → paste). At ~250k tokens, hand off rather than riding autocompact.

- API rejects missing or mismatched completion acknowledgments.

No public writer RPC, frontend switch, or backend deployment.** See [foundation readiness and limits](2026-09-30-timed-pt-foundation-readiness.md). Ticket #167 remains open. This expands [the proposed timed-write contract](2026-09-30-timed-write-contract.md); that contract\'s live metadata evidence and deployment approval requirements still apply.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe first backend release should cover PrepTest parent state, LR legs, RC legs, and the break together. Standalone timed LR/RC follows as a separate adoption phase. A parent-only RPC would leave the child-write race intact.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The existing boundaries determine the first batch\\r\\n\\r\\n| Existing boundary | Current behavior | Required v1 replacement |\\r\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestStore.ts` | Parent creation, revision CAS, device claim, pending device copies | Versioned create/claim commands and authoritative command responses; existing reads and backup ownership checks remain |\\r\\n| `src/lib/drillResumeSession.ts` | Separate parent-device check, then official LR KV snapshot upsert | LR snapshot checkpoint under the parent lock; retained device copy until acknowledgement |\\r\\n| `src/pages/Drill.tsx`, `src/lib/sectionHistorySave.ts` | LR closeout writes attempts, WAJ, history, resume completion in separate requests | One official close-leg command; explicit projection completion contract |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/api/rcProgress.ts` | Session creation, answer insert, clock/position update, and completion each check/write separately | Typed RC start/checkpoint/close-leg commands |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/pages/RcPlayer.tsx` | Questions and clock gated on account reads/saves; closeout writes blank first-attempt rows | Consume acknowledged session/position/clock; closeout batch and parent advance commit together |\\r\\n| `src/pages/PracticeTestRun.tsx` | Reads child results and later saves parent advancement/break/final score | Read authoritative parent returned by close-leg; parent and break commands cannot accept arbitrary JSON patches |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestRunner.ts`, `src/lib/practiceTestReview.ts` | Read attributed historical LR/RC records | Preserve result/review reads; v1 completion is not inferred from a child row that has not committed parent advancement |\\r\\n\\r\\nRepository schema is concrete but is not a fresh live DDL verification. `practice_test_runs.id` is **text**, not UUID. Its statuses are `in-progress`, `complete`, `abandoned`; RC uses `in_progress`, `completed`, `abandoned`. LR official records are JSON in `bootcamp_kv`, under `practice_sessions`; do not assume a normalized LR sessions table exists. Keep the installed owner FKs and per-leg/first-attempt unique indexes described in the contract.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 0: freeze behavior and reproduce the races\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepare an ordinary-authenticated two-client harness against an isolated database with the installed schema. Refresh the live metadata inventory before deployment. Exercise existing parent CAS, then demonstrate that separate child preflight/writes can race takeover. No service-role success is permission evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\nRecord these current semantics before implementation:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Parent `section_seconds` freezes the user\'s chosen timing. The break is 600 seconds. Historical null timing retains existing reader compatibility.\\r\\n- LR permits overtime and records `regulation_answered_qids`. Preserve that distinction; do not silently introduce automatic submission at budget expiry.\\r\\n- RC answer column is `selected`; null closeout rows count as unanswered, and session elapsed time is not the sum of per-question times.\\r\\n- Current scoring is client-derived. This work protects transactional ownership, clock state, and acknowledged results. It does **not** introduce a new secure-grade product requirement or claim server-verified answer correctness. Validate result structure and derive parent totals from acknowledged child results. Preserve existing scoring formulas and explicitly retain their trust boundary.\\r\\n- Current LR closeout requires its expected WAJ work before the leg is considered finished. Do not move it after advancement without a separately recorded change to that behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 1: add protected control state and receipts\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepare two forward migrations, not a historical-record rewrite:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_timed_work_v1_control.sql`: control fields, receipt table, typed RPC helpers, and owner result reads.\\r\\n2. `supabase/migrations/<timestamp>_timed_work_v1_enforcement.sql`: v1 direct-write restrictions and exhaustive OLD/NEW attribution protection.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe exact timestamps are assigned when implementation starts. Keep deployment of enforcement and adapter activation coordinated; an RPC left beside unrestricted protected raw writes does not provide the guarantee.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor the PT phase add nullable `timed_contract_version` to `practice_test_runs`, plus server-owned writer epoch, phase, accumulated elapsed milliseconds, running anchor, lease expiry, and active clock leg. Keep existing `revision` as the single command CAS version. Preserve existing device ID for UI display; possession of an arbitrary device ID alone does not authorize a write. Epoch/lease/revision are validated under the parent lock.\\r\\n\\r\\nConstraints for protected rows:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Version is supported; revision/epoch/elapsed are nonnegative.\\r\\n- Running phases have an anchor and lease; paused/terminal phases have no running anchor.\\r\\n- Clock leg matches the current frozen leg, or the phase is the one permitted break.\\r\\n- Owner, PT, pace, section duration, frozen leg definition, and protected version cannot be changed by a client patch.\\r\\n- Terminal state cannot reopen. No protected source or completion record is deleted by this API.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a companion binding table for LR KV records. Its owner/run/leg, namespace, record ID, and frozen queue identity are immutable, and there is one binding per PT LR leg. The existing key `drill::practice-test::<runId>::leg-<index>` and `practiceSessionIdFor` can be preserved for PT compatibility. A generic owner JSON blob must not become writer/access authority.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a durable command receipt table with unique `(owner_id, work_kind, work_id, command_id)`, canonical payload hash, committed revision, and committed result. A command UUID is separate from an RC attempt UUID. Store receipts in the same transaction as progress. Authenticated clients can read their own receipts but cannot insert/update/delete them directly. Retain receipts long enough for supported recovery; a TTL policy is not part of this batch.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 2: implement one typed PT transaction\\r\\n\\r\\nPublic entry points: `create_timed_practice_test_v1` and `commit_timed_work_v1`. Creation cannot take an arbitrary owner. New protected children are created inside start-leg, not by direct browser inserts.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe commit envelope is `{workKind, workId, expectedRevision, writerEpoch, deviceId, commandId, operation, payload}`. Derive owner from `auth.uid()`. Parse only the fields for the named operation and reject unknown/immutable patches. Start with PT operations: claim/adopt, start-leg, checkpoint, pause, resume, close-leg, start-break, finish-break, abandon. Final completion is derived when the final leg closes; there is no unrestricted set-score or set-current-leg operation.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach successful command performs these steps:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Resolve the actor-owned parent and lock it `FOR UPDATE`. Look for the command receipt under that lock. A matching receipt acknowledges the old committed operation before stale-revision or current-access rejection; changed payload rejects. Return both the receipt and **current** authoritative parent so retrying an old receipt cannot restore an older UI state.\\r\\n2. Validate supported version, expected revision, writer epoch, lease, exact phase/leg, and immutable child binding. A new stale command returns a typed conflict with current state and makes no progress writes.\\r\\n3. Check current PT entitlement using the existing `can_sit_practice_test` rules. Lock the actual grant row used for authorization: [REDACTED] profile feature row, exact owned/unlocked/nonarchived assignment, or admin-role row. A boolean precheck alone does not serialize a concurrent revoke. Use deterministic lock order and test it against the revocation paths. Missing access rejects new writes while preserving history and receipts.\\r\\n4. Settle clock time using server time, bounded by the acknowledged lease expiry, then apply the operation. Never decrease elapsed time. Heartbeat renews only a valid active writer. Proposed 15-second heartbeat/45-second lease remains a proposal to verify, not an adopted product constant.\\r\\n5. Persist LR snapshot or RC answer batch together with elapsed time and position. Validate qid membership, queue order, question count, selected letters/nulls, index bounds, and exact parent/leg/session attribution. Do not regenerate missing content or accept a new queue during recovery. Keep all acknowledged choices through takeover.\\r\\n6. On close-leg, persist the official child result, required closeout projections, child terminal state, parent leg result, and advance/break/final state in one transaction. Increment parent revision once, write receipt, and return parent plus child checkpoint and server time.\\r\\n\\r\\nRC retains existing first-attempt uniqueness. Same attempt UUID with the same owner/session/question/passage/choice is idempotent; different content rejects. A different first-attempt UUID for an already committed question conflicts rather than replacing the original. Review reanswers require their separate allowed semantics and cannot reopen an exam leg. Clock checkpoint and answer acknowledgement must share the command; current split calls are not enough.\\r\\n\\r\\nLR stores the frozen `PracticeSession` shape and validates stable attribution outside that JSON. Do not trust supplied `user_id`, `pool_slug`, `completion_id`, or arbitrary section-history parent links. Keep unanswered/answered/overtime distinctions and current score trust. Validate totals against the frozen queue and derive parent aggregation from the acknowledged child record rather than a later unrelated readback.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor LR WAJ/analytics, inventory `commitSessionAttempts`, `logSectionWrongAnswers`, and `persistSectionResults` before moving their writes. Either put mandatory rows in the transaction, or introduce an explicit closeout-pending phase with an idempotent transactionally enqueued projection job. In the latter design, parent advancement still waits for required projection acknowledgement. Mail remains optional and cannot block the official leg, matching current behavior. Do not leave the existing client closeout path writing official rows around the RPC.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 3: close direct-write bypasses before switching clients\\r\\n\\r\\nProtected parent INSERT/UPDATE, attributed LR KV INSERT/UPDATE, RC session/attempt INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and official section-result INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE must reject ordinary authenticated direct mutations. Restrict metadata-only RC operations deliberately rather than accidentally disabling exclusions/review flags. Preserve ordinary bootcamp data and historical reads.\\r\\n\\r\\nEnforcement checks **OLD and NEW** protection, owner, source identity, and attribution. Clearing the PT FK, setting contract version null, moving a protected KV record, or inserting an alternate child for the same protected leg cannot escape it. Reserved PT LR source keys cannot be recreated through generic KV writes. Replace conflicting permissive policies; adding a stricter permissive policy leaves the existing owner policy effective.\\r\\n\\r\\nPrefer a dedicated tightly privileged no-login executor role for protected RPCs if Lovable\'s managed migration role supports that ownership setup. Authenticated/anonymous must have no membership in it. Security-definer functions fix search path, qualify tables, check `auth.uid()`, and receive only narrow grants. Ordinary callers must not be able to forge an RPC-only bypass with a custom setting. Verify managed-role capabilities before selecting an enforcement technique; do not equate every `postgres`-owned definer function with this authorized writer.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 4: switch PT adapters and explicitly adopt active work\\r\\n\\r\\nAdd `src/lib/timedWorkClient.ts` for typed command envelopes/responses and conflict/access/expired-writer errors. Backups retain the same pending command UUID, payload, expected revision, and epoch until acknowledged. Never mint a fresh command on a lost-response retry.\\r\\n\\r\\nSwitch the existing boundaries in the first table. The parent returned by close-leg drives advancement; `PracticeTestRun.tsx` stops performing a second parent save for that v1 leg. `RcPlayer.tsx` and `Drill.tsx` stop clocks and hide/gate questions on loss of authoritative writer state until claim/recovery is acknowledged. Break pause/resume/finish uses the same contract. Device elapsed time is recovery evidence, not server proof of an instantaneous offline pause.\\r\\n\\r\\nNew PTs use v1 only after backend readiness is verified. Existing active rows enter through explicit adoption/claim under the parent lock. Validate and preserve owner, current leg, frozen queue/passages, acknowledged answers, saved position, timing, and terminal results. Adopt only a known server-owned child; unknown or contradictory device-only copies need explicit recovery rather than automatic import. Already completed/abandoned rows remain readable and are not rewritten.\\r\\n\\r\\nAn old browser meeting an adopted record must fail its raw writes and require refresh. Compatibility tests must include bypass attempts through every legacy writer, not only the new adapter\'s happy path.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Phase 5: give standalone LR/RC durable sitting identities\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not include this in the initial PT rollout. Standalone LR currently uses `drill::section::ptX-sY` with a deterministic record ID; retakes overwrite that identity. A control row keyed only to it would confuse terminal history with a new sitting.\\r\\n\\r\\nIntroduce a distinct v1 sitting UUID and immutable control/source identity. Use a distinct v1 LR KV record per sitting plus a current-active lookup, or normalized canonical snapshot storage. A unique active `(owner, source_kind, source_key)` permits one active writer while retaining completed retakes. RC already has a session UUID, but it still needs frozen standalone source authorization and control binding.\\r\\n\\r\\nInventory every supported standalone source before enforcement: feature-granted manual full section, exact classroom/homework assignment, bootcamp source, and any supported custom timed source. Freeze source identity and check its current ownership/unlock/archive state on every command. Unsupported source kinds fail explicitly. Broad access can authorize its supported source kinds; an unrelated assignment cannot authorize an arbitrary queue. Retain existing timing/retake behavior and clearly identify any temporarily excluded legacy paths.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Code prepared is separate from deployed and verified\\r\\n\\r\\nImplementation deliverables before approval:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Reviewed additive schema/RPC and enforcement migrations, with immutable/terminal/owner constraints and a rollback-free forward recovery plan.\\r\\n- An isolated PostgreSQL transaction harness covering same-revision races, save-versus-takeover, save-versus-revoke, changed-payload replay, old-receipt replay after later work, lease expiry, failed closeout, and raw OLD/NEW attribution bypasses.\\r\\n- Frontend adapter tests for pending command retention, authoritative response consumption, no duplicate advancement, older clients, adoption, failed hydration, and frozen queues.\\r\\n- Typecheck/build and student/teacher browser evidence before frontend release.\\r\\n\\r\\nRefresh live metadata immediately before deployment. Joshua must confirm the Lovable Cloud backend route and immediately approve any credit-using action. No Supabase CLI Edge Function deployment under the current managed backend. Generate database types only from the deployed schema; temporary typed RPC boundaries may be isolated in the new client until regeneration, not hand edits to generated types.\\r\\n\\r\\nReport four separate states: **code prepared**, **backend deployed**, **frontend switched**, **live acceptance verified**. Run ordinary authenticated two-device/outage/revocation acceptance for PT LR, PT RC, and break before expanding rollout. Later run standalone LR/RC separately. Keep #167 open while any supported active path lacks the contract or its acceptance evidence.\\r\\n"}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"dd7db8","wall_time_seconds":1.4758265,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":5119,"output":"# Timed work must commit through one account transaction\\r\\n\\r\\nDate: 2026-09-30\\r\\n\\r\\nStatus: **Proposed implementation contract. Not implemented or deployed.** This is the backend follow-up for competitor-audit ticket #167. It does not close #167 or claim full second-device, outage, or revoked-access acceptance. The frontend recovery fixes can ship independently.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Why the existing saves leave a race\\r\\n\\r\\nThe parent PrepTest save already compares revision, active device, and in-progress status in one conditional UPDATE. Its LR and RC children check the parent separately before writing their own rows. A second browser can take over after that check and before the child write. Browser-local write queues do not serialize two devices. Ownership RLS prevents writing another student\'s work; it does not prevent an old browser from writing the same student\'s work.\\r\\n\\r\\nEvidence in this first table is from repository source. **SQL files describe intended schema, not verified live DDL.** The next section separately records a live metadata inspection on 2026-09-30. Neither metadata inspection nor a successful ordinary save proves a two-device race test passed. Record an independent authenticated CAS test before rollout.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Source | Existing behavior and limitation |\\r\\n| --- | --- |\\r\\n| `src/lib/practiceTestStore.ts:271`, `:302`, `:244` | `saveAccountPracticeTestRun` conditionally writes parent revision/device/status; `continueAccountPracticeTestHere` claims the device with parent CAS. `isActivePracticeTestDevice` is a separate read used by child writers. |\\r\\n| `src/lib/drillResumeSession.ts:56`, `:76` | `assertActiveTestLeg` checks the parent device; `syncSectionToAccount` separately upserts the LR frozen snapshot into `bootcamp_kv`. Official section writes have local serialization and recovery copies. |\\r\\n| `src/features/rc/api/rcProgress.ts:93`, `:154`, `:228`, `:184` | `assertActivePracticeTestSession`, `writeSessionClock`, `recordAttempt`, and `completeSession` use separate parent reads and child writes. RC clock serialization is per browser. |\\r\\n| `src/pages/PracticeTestRun.tsx:380`, `:388` | The parent stores break start time; failed-save recovery freezes remaining time locally. The break heartbeat currently runs at 15 seconds. |\\r\\n| `src/components/AssignmentGate.tsx:32`, `:299` | Route admission accepts a feature flag or item authorization, with cached assignment reads. It is not a server write contract and cannot provide immediate revocation enforcement. |\\r\\n| `supabase/migrations/20260829120000_practice_test_runs.sql:135`, `:237`, `:245`, `:249`, `:281` | Parent owner UPDATE, RC owner FK, one LR result/RC session per leg, and RC first-attempt uniqueness. Owner UPDATE does not enforce terminal transitions, device ownership, or current access. |\\r\\n| `supabase/migrations/20260927010000_practice_test_account_sync.sql:3` | Adds `section_seconds` and `active_device_id`. Does not add a clock lease or transactional child writes. |\\r\\n| `supabase/migrations/20260923010300_practice_test_assignments.sql:41`, `:63` | Defines `can_sit_practice_test` and applies it to parent INSERT. Existing owner UPDATE remains broader. |\\r\\n| `supabase/migrations/20260603142340_2aa5f9d2-63ec-4736-af91-7a426457f9de.sql:31` | KV owner UPDATE permits account-owned JSON snapshots without active-leg or lease checks. |\\r\\n| `supabase/migrations/20260806000000_rc_drilling.sql:35` | RC owner policies scope work to the owner. They do not implement clock/device/access state transitions. |\\r\\n\\r\\nReuse these tables and constraints. The existing `abandon_stale_practice_tests` RPC is cleanup, not an atomic checkpoint API. No relevant timed checkpoint RPC was found in these files.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Live metadata confirms the child-write gap\\r\\n\\r\\nOn **2026-09-30**, read-only Lovable `query_database` SELECTs inspected PostgreSQL catalogs for project `53b9a6f2-aba7-4ae4-8dd1-fa5b8aab4d76`. Database status was enabled with Supabase stack. The queries read schema metadata only: no student rows, seeds, credentials, DDL, or mutations. They covered `pg_policies`, `information_schema.columns`, `pg_constraint`, `pg_indexes`, non-internal `pg_trigger`, relevant `pg_proc`, RLS flags, and ordinary-role table grants.\\r\\n\\r\\nConfirmed installed:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `practice_test_runs` has `revision integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, nullable `active_device_id text`, nullable positive `section_seconds integer`, break fields, and existing parent status constraints. No lease/epoch/clock-state/contract-version columns were present.\\r\\n- `bootcamp_kv` has exactly owner, namespace, record ID, JSON data, and updated timestamp columns. There is no separate writer revision/lease field.\\r\\n- RC sessions have parent run/leg attribution and nullable completion time. RC attempts have UUID primary key, session/owner/question identity and first-attempt flag. Neither table has a writer revision/epoch/lease column.\\r\\n- Composite ownership FKs `rc_sessions_pt_run_fk`, `rc_attempts_session_owner_fk`, and `section_history_pt_run_fk` are installed. RC and section-history attributed-leg pair checks are installed.\\r\\n- Unique partial indexes `rc_sessions_pt_leg_once`, `section_history_pt_leg_once`, and `rc_attempts_first_once` are installed. These prevent duplicate leg rows/first-attempt rows, not stale writer acceptance.\\r\\n- RLS is enabled on all four timed-progress tables. It is not FORCE RLS. Authenticated has INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT table privileges; policies determine which ordinary API operations succeed. Anonymous also has table grants, but owner checks still depend on `auth.uid()`; grants alone do not prove anonymous access.\\r\\n- The only non-internal triggers on the four progress tables and `section_history` are `bootcamp_kv_touch` and `practice_test_runs_touch`, both updated-timestamp triggers. No active-writer/access/terminal-state trigger was installed on these tables.\\r\\n- `can_sit_practice_test(_user uuid, _pt integer)` is installed as STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, checking admin, `profiles.has_practice_access`, or an owned nonarchived/unlocked exact PT assignment. `can_access_drill` was absent. The relevant function-name and function-body reference scan returned `can_sit_practice_test` and `abandon_stale_practice_tests`, plus timestamp triggers in the name scan; no checkpoint API appeared in that scoped inventory.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe following policy text is the narrow raw evidence returned by `pg_policies`. SQL formatting is preserved; `NULL` means that catalog field was null. Read policies are summarized afterward because they are not the mutation blocker.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Table / policy / command / roles | `qual` | `with_check` |\\r\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\r\\n| `practice_test_runs` / `pt_runs_owner_insert` / INSERT / `{public}` | NULL | `((user_id = auth.uid()) AND can_sit_practice_test(auth.uid(), pt))` |\\r\\n| `practice_test_runs` / `pt_runs_owner_update` / UPDATE / `{public}` | `(user_id = auth.uid())` | `(user_id = auth.uid())` |\\r\\n| `bootcamp_kv` / `Users insert own bootcamp data` / INSERT / `{authenticated}` | NULL | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` |\\r\\n| `bootcamp_kv` / `Users update own bootcamp data` / UPDATE / `{authenticated}` | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` |\\r\\n| `bootcamp_kv` / `Admins delete bootcamp data` / DELETE / `{authenticated}` | `has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'::app_role)` | NULL |\\r\\n| `rc_drill_sessions` / `own sessions` / ALL / `{public}` | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` |\\r\\n| `rc_attempts` / `own attempts` / ALL / `{public}` | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` | `(auth.uid() = user_id)` |\\r\\n\\r\\nOwn SELECT policies are installed for parent/KV. Admin SELECT policies named `admins_read_practice_test_runs`, `admins_read_bootcamp_kv`, `admins_read_rc_drill_sessions`, and `admins_read_rc_attempts` use `has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'::app_role)`. RC owner ALL policies include SELECT. No parent DELETE policy was returned.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Confirmed blocker:** live owner UPDATE/RC ALL policies contain no current-access, active-device, active-leg, revision, or terminal-state predicates. No relevant enforcement trigger supplies them. Existing ownership FKs and uniqueness constraints are stronger than a client-only ownership convention but do not close the parent-check/child-write race. Parent CAS remains implemented by the caller\'s conditional UPDATE, not required by a database policy. This establishes the live schema gap; it does not claim successful denial/race/revocation mutation tests.\\r\\n\\r\\n## One versioned command owns parent and child writes\\r\\n\\r\\nImplement `commit_timed_work_v1` as a database transaction. For a PrepTest, lock its existing `practice_test_runs` parent row. For standalone timed LR/RC, lock a small normalized `timed_work_controls` row keyed to the immutable owned LR snapshot or RC session identity. This companion row prevents generic KV JSON from becoming the source of device ownership or source authorization.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe command accepts a work identity, expected revision, writer epoch/token, command UUID, operation, and a typed operation payload. It does not accept an arbitrary student owner. Derive the actor from `auth.uid()`.\\r\\n\\r\\nAllowed operations: claim, start, checkpoint, pause, resume, complete, abandon; PrepTests additionally start/finish break and complete/advance leg. Validate each operation separately rather than accepting an unrestricted parent/JSON patch.\\r\\n\\r\\nWithin the transaction:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Lock the control/parent row for `auth.uid()` and validate contract version.\\r\\n2. Check current access against live source rows, expected revision, active writer epoch, allowed state transition, and exact current leg.\\r\\n3. Check child ownership and immutable source attribution. A PrepTest child must belong to this parent, owner, leg, section kind, and frozen section definition.\\r\\n4. Update the official LR frozen snapshot or the RC attempt, elapsed clock, and current position together with the control state. Reject missing/unavailable question identities rather than drawing a new queue.\\r\\n5. On completion, acknowledge the official result and advance the parent atomically. No next leg or final score becomes available before this transaction commits.\\r\\n6. Increment revision, store the command receipt, and return the authoritative control/parent plus child checkpoint and server time.\\r\\n\\r\\nMaintain durable command receipts keyed by owner, work identity, and command UUID, with a payload hash and committed result. Same UUID/same payload returns the acknowledged result after a lost response. Same UUID/different payload is rejected. Check a matching receipt before rejecting a replay for stale revision: a legitimately committed command remains acknowledged after later operations. A new stale command never overwrites newer work.\\r\\n\\r\\nLR analytics and WAJ remain projections of acknowledged work. If they cannot be written inside closeout, enqueue idempotent follow-up work transactionally and keep retries independent of whether the official leg can advance. RC attempts retain existing UUIDs and first-attempt uniqueness. Decide explicitly which projections must finish before results appear; do not silently weaken the current closeout contract.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Every save rechecks access without changing the actor\\r\\n\\r\\nPrepTest commands reuse `can_sit_practice_test(auth.uid(), parent.pt)`, including current unlock/archive state and the Practice tests feature flag. Validate the active exact leg independently of the feature flag. A broad feature grant does not authorize an arbitrary child under a different parent or leg.\\r\\n\\r\\nStandalone LR/RC control creation freezes its source discriminator and source identity. Each protected write requires the current drill feature grant or a current, owned assignment that authorizes exactly that section/session source. Validate unlock/archive/deletion state and source membership server-side. Opening unrelated assigned work must not grant access to arbitrary sections. Do not infer authorization from a caller-supplied queue, generic KV namespace, or cached route result.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe standalone source mapping must be inventoried and implemented for every supported launch before enforcement is enabled. Unsupported source kinds fail explicitly. Teacher/admin read access continues through existing SELECT policies. No teacher mutation impersonates the student\'s writer; any future teacher recovery operation needs its own audited authorization contract.\\r\\n\\r\\nAccess revocation denies new checkpoint, resume, claim, and completion commands. Preserve prior answers and recovery copies. Historical owned result reads remain available according to the existing result-access policy. Retrying an already committed command can acknowledge its existing receipt but cannot create further work after revocation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The server needs a clock and an expiring writer lease\\r\\n\\r\\nStore phase, accumulated elapsed milliseconds, server running anchor, lease expiry, writer epoch, and contract version. For PrepTests the clock state identifies the exact leg or break; section duration remains the frozen `section_seconds` chosen at creation. Standalone controls hold their own frozen timing. Use server time for accepted state transitions; never replace saved time with a smaller client value.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Proposed, not locked:** heartbeat every 15 seconds, writer lease 45 seconds. This follows the current break heartbeat cadence and tolerates two missed heartbeats before expiry. It bounds stale-writer acceptance and server-visible disconnect behavior without treating a single transient request failure as a permanent takeover. Verify the tolerance against real latency and teaching requirements before adopting it.\\r\\n\\r\\nA successful pause checkpoints elapsed time and removes the running anchor. Resume creates a new anchor only after acknowledgment. When the lease expires, the authoritative clock stops at its expiry boundary and the work requires explicit recovery/claim. A claim increments the writer epoch so all old in-flight writes are rejected under the same parent lock.\\r\\n\\r\\n**An offline pause that never reaches the server cannot be globally instantaneous.** Another device can only observe the last acknowledged checkpoint and lease expiry. Document that interval in acceptance evidence. A local paused clock remains a recovery copy, not proof that the server paused at the same instant. Reconcile unacknowledged elapsed time deliberately and monotonically; do not auto-replay local answers over a newer writer\'s work.\\r\\n\\r\\nAn explicit takeover may invalidate an unexpired lease if the existing UX permits it. The command must still CAS the latest revision and increment the epoch atomically. Expiry must never reset timing or grant a fresh question queue.\\r\\n\\r\\n## RPC adoption must also close direct-write bypasses\\r\\n\\r\\nFor protected contract-version rows, deny authenticated direct parent UPDATE and direct writes to attributed LR KV records, RC session/attempt rows, and official section results. Cover INSERT as well as UPDATE so a caller cannot recreate a child under a new identity. Apply the rule to the OLD row as well as NEW attribution so clearing a protected foreign key cannot bypass enforcement.\\r\\n\\r\\nAn RPC alone is insufficient while broad owner policies still allow the same writes. Permissive policies are ORed; inspect and replace conflicting policies rather than adding a stricter policy beside them. Keep ordinary non-timed/non-protected bootcamp progress behavior intact.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse tightly scoped security-definer functions only where required to perform these protected writes. Restrict execution to authenticated callers, fix the search path, qualify objects, and explicitly verify `auth.uid()`, ownership, source access, writer epoch, and operation payload. No service-role credential goes to the browser. A transaction-local enforcement mechanism, if used, must not be forgeable by authenticated callers.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Roll out without erasing old sittings\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Refresh the live metadata inventory recorded above immediately before deployment. Verify the existing parent CAS with two ordinary authenticated clients. Record differences from repository SQL before applying changes.\\r\\n2. Add nullable/versioned clock state, standalone control rows, command receipts, and RPCs. Leave historical completed records readable and do not rewrite their timing or answers.\\r\\n3. Add frontend adapters that consume authoritative RPC responses. New timed work uses contract v1. Existing active work enters through an explicit adoption/claim transaction that preserves owner, frozen queue, acknowledged answers, current position, accommodation timing, and completion state.\\r\\n4. Enable protected direct-write restrictions for v1 work. Old browser clients encountering adopted work must fail safely and require refresh; they cannot keep using the legacy writer.\\r\\n5. Complete race, outage, revocation, and compatibility acceptance before widening adoption. No terminal-state reopening, deletion, synthetic timestamps, or silent conversion of an unknown-owner device copy.\\r\\n\\r\\nLegacy active work still using the old protocol does not carry the new cross-device guarantee. Keep #167 open until its supported active paths have adopted the contract or are explicitly excluded with truthful UI behavior. Deploy forward; never roll main back to bypass enforcement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Acceptance proves the transaction rather than the happy path\\r\\n\\r\\n| Scenario | Required result |\\r\\n| --- | --- |\\r\\n| Two clients submit the same expected revision | Exactly one new command commits; the other gets conflict with authoritative state. |\\r\\n| Takeover races an LR/RC save | Parent lock and epoch decide order; no old-writer child commit after successful takeover. |\\r\\n| Direct protected INSERT/UPDATE or attribution clearing | Denied for ordinary authenticated owner and other account. |\\r\\n| Old epoch, wrong owner/source/leg, terminal parent | No child or parent mutation; saved work remains intact. |\\r\\n| Access is revoked after route admission | New checkpoint/claim/resume/completion denied despite cached route authorization. |\\r\\n| Response lost after commit | Same command UUID/payload returns one acknowledged answer/position/result without duplicate advancement. |\\r\\n| Replayed UUID with changed payload | Rejected; acknowledged receipt and result unchanged. |\\r\\n| A later valid command precedes retry of an old receipt | Old committed operation is acknowledged without restoring its older state. |\\r\\n| RC first-attempt insert races | One first attempt per session/question, UUID retries preserve the original answer. |\\r\\n| Pause/break save fails, reload, then second-device claim | Account clock/lease state is consistent; local backup cannot silently reset remaining time. |\\r\\n| Unsent offline pause | Server stops at documented expiry boundary; no claim of immediate global pause. |\\r\\n| Lost heartbeat and stale browser return | Questions remain gated until claim/recovery acknowledgment; elapsed time does not decrease. |\\r\\n| Leg closeout or final-score write fails midway | No partial advance/score; retry finishes the same leg exactly once. |\\r\\n| Older frontend resumes adopted work | Protected raw writes fail safely; refresh preserves acknowledged records. |\\r\\n| Teacher views records | Same owner/source work is visible through allowed reads; teacher identity never becomes the student writer. |\\r\\n\\r\\nTest standalone LR and standalone RC separately from PrepTest LR/RC and the break. Use existing owned tester fixtures, ordinary authenticated accounts, and controlled request failures. ## assistant

The transport now preserves one pending command per owner and run, and refuses to send unless the server advertises v1 support. I’m adding tests for lost replies, mismatched receipts, stale responses, and account changes before integrating the exact LR/RC payload schemas.

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/docs/implementation-plans/2026-09-30-timed-client-adapter-readiness.md\n+# The v1 client and parent adapter are prepared, without activation\n+\n+Date: 2026-09-30.\n+\n+`src/lib/timedWorkClient.ts` implements the isolated ordinary-auth RPC transport and durable command queue. `src/lib/timedPracticeTestStore.ts` prepares the parent conversion, control commands, lease-bounded display clock, and exact child launch metadata. Existing parent, LR, RC, and route writers remain untouched by these files.\n+\n+The owner/run queue keeps the original command UUID, operation, payload, expected revision, writer epoch, and original parent until acknowledgment. A lost reply, write denial, account change, or storage acknowledgment failure preserves that command. A second command cannot replace it. Recovery is deliberate through `retry()`, with no automatic command rebasing or legacy raw-write fallback.\n+\n+`prepare()` checks the ordinary actor and operation payload before preserving a request. `retry()` checks the actor before capability discovery, before the command, and after its reply. Unsupported version, missing capability, inactive mutation capability, or an unadvertised operation blocks writes. The RPC entry points are `create_timed_practice_test_v1(p_command)` and `commit_timed_work_v1(p_command)`. Public operation payloads match the SQL writer, including the empty-payload `heartbeat` for running sections and breaks.\n+\n+The acknowledgment must bind owner, work kind, run, command UUID, operation, full original envelope, and the exact committed revision. The current parent must carry protected v1 control fields and the same immutable full content manifest/hash, section budget, lease budget, and frozen leg definitions. Current checkpoint attribution and ordered LR queue or RC passages are checked against that parent. Old receipts can acknowledge their original command while returning newer authority; a delayed older parent does not overwrite a newer saved parent or checkpoint.\n+\n+`refresh()` reads `read_timed_practice_test_v1(p_work_id)` as one owner-safe account snapshot. Read capability remains available for protected history while mutation capability is disabled. Reads preserve the pending envelope and its original authority, so a later leg cannot reinterpret a lost-reply checkpoint as a new command. The latest received receipt is retained with the acknowledged parent.\n+\n+The parent adapter maps authoritative identity, timing accommodation, device/revision, leg results, and break state to `PracticeTestRun`. It does not adopt or rewrite legacy rows. Its clock is a display estimate anchored to server time, bounded at the acknowledged lease expiry; it does not claim an offline pause reached the server. Pending recovery, a different device, or expiry blocks child launch. Missing or contradictory frozen child content fails instead of generating a replacement queue.\n+\n+Validation: focused transport/parent tests and changed-file ESLint pass; full application typecheck passes. These tests use mocked ordinary-auth transport responses and browser storage. They establish client boundary behavior, not deployed backend transaction or production acceptance evidence. The separate real PostgreSQL harness owns backend evidence.\n+\n+Remaining gates: independent SQL/transport review, coordinated LR/RC adapters, explicit rollout/adoption policy, ordinary two-device/outage/revocation acceptance, and backend readiness before any frontend switch. No backend deployment, frontend activation, live writes, or credit-spending action was performed by this client slice.\n*** End Patch"));
